items.title: uk-insolvency: a Gazette data.json body that arrives empty or shorter than its content-length is retried like a 5xx and, after the retries, keeps the previous snapshot without an error row
items.why: Daily numbers 2026-09-30: `uk-insolvency (thegazette.co.uk page results-page=1: Unexpected end of JSON input after 3 reads (0 bytes, content-length declared))`; 09-28 the same `Unexpected end of JSON input`; 09-27 and 09-29 a 500 (retry shipped 09-29, `gazette-5xx-retry`). Four days without a fresh insolvency snapshot on a live surface. The source (`src/sources/uk-insolvency.ts`) already reads the body up to three times; a zero-byte body with a declared content-length is the origin closing the stream early, so: treat a short body exactly like a 5xx (fair-use pause, one more read), and when every read fails, log `refresh_log` status `skipped` with the message and keep the previous KV snapshot (Blind Mode already serves it) rather than `error`, so the row shows a stale-since date instead of a daily error. Verify the current response shape through the relay first (`GET RANGE=0-4095` of the data.json URL with the corporate notice types). Id follows the `refresh-<slug>` convention of scripts/refresh-errors-to-queue.ts so the 06:30 job extends this item instead of filing a second one. Built 2026-09-30 (burn-down): relay check showed the Gazette serving the full 204 KB page-1 body (100 notices) to a runner while the Worker read 0 bytes, so the cut is momentary and size-related: page size 50, a cut body (empty or shorter than content-length) retried four times with growing fair-use pauses (~13 s), and a later page that never arrives keeps the pages already read (warn `partial_snapshot`) instead of failing the day. The `skipped` refresh_log status is NOT added: the table's CHECK allows only ok/error (a migration for a rebuild) and the error row is exactly what `refresh-errors-to-queue` keys on — hiding it would hide the outage. KV keeps a stale snapshot 7 days, so the 2026-09-26 snapshot expires ~10-03 without a good refresh.

items.title: Keep a paused source's last snapshot alive: a failed refresh with a snapshot in KV re-puts the snapshot and its stats blob with a fresh TTL, /stats/<slug> renders the dated notice when the blob is gone instead of a 503, and the MCP/REST 'temporarily unavailable' answer for a source with a `notice` carries that notice
items.why: Research 2026-10-17 (relay gankdat-research-2026-10-17): /v1/health has uk-planning last refreshed 2026-10-09 05:01 (187 h), GET /stats/uk-planning answers 503 'Statistics are being prepared' and the 10-16 Daily numbers row's MCP probe got `tool error: Source 'uk-planning' is temporarily unavailable` on both passes — the keyless call every directory health check makes, on the first listed tool. Cause in code: cache.ts keeps a KV snapshot for cacheTtlSeconds × 7 = 7 days for uk-planning (86,400 s TTL) and the 05:00 wave's refresh throws before writing anything (`origin dataset empty`, by design since the 10-11 decision), so the 10-09 snapshot and the stats blob expired on 10-16 ~05:00 and nothing re-wrote them: readCached has no hit to serve stale, every query 503s, the Apify actor uk-planning-applications (19 runs/30d by others) now fails each run (Apify's QA will flag it within days, third maintenance flag), the indexed /stats page is a JSON 503 and the §7 60-day customer-query clock set on 10-11 cannot be read because nobody can call the dataset. The 10-11 decision ('the last snapshot stays served') assumed retention it did not have. Do: in store.ts refreshOne / cache.ts, when a KV source's refresh fails and a snapshot exists, re-put data + stats keys with snapshotTtlSeconds (a touch, no origin read; log `event: snapshot_retained`); render /stats/<slug> from the snapshot or at least the notice + last_refreshed_at when the blob is missing for a source with `notice`; make the 503/tool-error message for a `notice` source say the notice (agents and the probe then read the cause, not 'retry later'). Score 7: evidence 3 (live 503 on an indexed page, probe red two passes, an Apify actor with outside users failing) × reach 2 (every shelf that lists uk-planning: REST, MCP directories, Apify, x402) ÷ 0.3 day. Built 2026-10-17 (burn-down): cache.ts retainSnapshot re-puts the data and stats keys with a fresh TTL after every failed KV refresh (no origin read; `snapshot_retained` log event); store.ts unavailableMessage puts the origin notice in the REST 503 and both MCP tool errors; the query tool description ends with `Origin notice: …` and scripts/mcp-probe.ts pickTool skips such a tool, so the probe reads a live source; /stats/<slug> with no blob and a notice renders a 200 page with the notice. 4 tests. Proof amended: uk-planning's snapshot was already gone before the fix and cannot be re-created (the origin is empty), so `call 200` on the probe comes from it picking uk-tenders, not from uk-planning serving data; the retention proof is the next paused source keeping its snapshot past 7 days, and /stats/uk-planning answering 200 with the notice through the relay.

items.title: uk-trademark-journal: third silent-night streak since 10-04 (no refresh_log row 10-15, 10-16 after ok 10-14 06:10) — read the wave outcome, find why wave 7 dies on three nights in four, fix so every night writes a row
items.why: Research 2026-10-17: /v1/health (relay gankdat-research-2026-10-17) has the journal last refreshed 2026-10-14 06:10:42; the 10-16 row says `no successful refresh since 2026-10-14` with no error and no skipped row, so wave 7 wrote nothing on 10-15 and 10-16, and the 24-h wave log for the slug has no line from the wave (metrics run 38866226604). Pattern since the 10-09 materialised-CTE fix: ok 10-10 (5 min 56 s into the wave), silent 10-11, 10-12, 10-13, ok 10-14 (5 min 42 s), silent 10-15, 10-16 — a success every fourth night, the ok nights finishing well inside the 15-minute budget. Two facet pages (/stats/uk-trademark-journal/class/35, /class/18) logged `[error]` on 10-15/16, consistent with the facet blobs ageing out while the refresh never completes. Hypotheses to test, in order: (a) a night with a new weekly issue to download (DOWNLOAD_BUDGET_MS 6 min) plus the 162k-row delta plus the 45-class facet aggregation (4-min budget) exceeds the Cron Trigger's CPU or wall limit and the isolate is killed before any row — the next nights load the cached issue (`tmj:issue:*`) and should be faster, which they are not; (b) memory: parsing a full XML issue and holding the (seq, id, hash) index of 162k rows in one isolate exceeds 128 MB (an exceededMemory outcome, no log line); (c) the trigger itself not firing (the `schedules.mjs reset` step shows 7 triggers in sync, so unlikely). First step: the cron-outcome reading (wave-log-cron-outcome-reading) or, sooner, the Workers observability query for `$workers.event.cron = '5 6 * * *'` run by hand from a session with the token. Fix candidates: split wave 7 into download+parse (writes the KV issue cache and a `skipped` row) and delta+facets on the next trigger; or give the journal a wave of its own at 06:20 for facets. Filed under the auto-filer's id pattern so the 10-17 row extends this item instead of filing a duplicate. Dated 2026-10-18 by burn-down 2026-10-17 01:25: its first step, the wave's cron outcome, is read by the 10-17 metrics row (reading built this night, `wave 06:05: <outcome>`); diagnosing before that row exists is the guessing this item exists to end. Built 2026-10-18 (build): the 10-17 and 10-18 Daily numbers rows list no stale journal — wave 7 wrote `ok` rows both nights, so the cron-outcome reading never ran for it; and the 10-16 metrics job log (run 38866226604) shows the observability query returned not one line from ANY cron wave in 24 h — no `refresh_wave`, no `refresh_failed` for uk-planning, though wave 1 verifiably ran (14 sources refreshed in 26 h) — so Worker logs cannot diagnose a silent night from a sandbox or the runner. Fix built in-band instead: `src/sources/progress.ts` — every attempt puts `refresh:progress:<slug>` at start and at each phase (backfill, index, stream N records, written, stats), clears it after its own row; a marker still there when the next attempt starts becomes the missing `error` row `silent refresh started <when> died after <phase> <detail> at <s> s, no row written`, so a killed night has a row the next morning and the Daily numbers row names the phase. Also: the `ok` row is written before the best-effort stats/facets in all three paths (a wave killed inside the 45-class facet aggregation keeps its row), and the journal's issue fetch carries a 5-minute `AbortSignal.timeout` (a hung IPO request was the one silent cause the source could name). Root cause still open: the follow-up item reads the first `silent refresh` row.

items.title: live /mcp has failed the CI probe 2 times in the last 4 days — find what answers a directory's initialize / tools/list / tools/call with an error and fix it
items.why: Filed by the 06:30 metrics job (scripts/refresh-errors-to-queue.ts): the Daily numbers rows list mcp-probe under refresh errors on 2026-10-16 (call 200 (tool error: Source 'uk-planning' is temporarily unavailable; retry later); authe) and 2026-10-18: call n/a (The operation was aborted due to timeout). The probe (scripts/mcp-probe.ts, from the metrics runner) is what Glama, Smithery and the Claude directory see; every directory ranks an erroring server below healthy ones. The step and status are in the message; reproduce it against the local Worker (test/mcp-directory.spec.ts) with the same request, read `/v1/health` through the relay, and fix the Worker — not the probe. Built 2026-10-18 (build): the two failures had different causes. 10-16 was uk-planning's expired snapshot (fixed 10-17: probe skips a paused tool, snapshot retained). 10-18 (metrics run 39106552120, probe step 07:10:18–07:10:42): keyless tools/call on query_uk_tenders timed out at 20 s, the keyed call right after answered 200; /v1/health via relay mcp-probe-health-2026-10-18 has uk-tenders refreshed 05:01:06 that morning (snapshot fresh, 1,000 rows, cpu_ms 300000), and the Worker live at 07:10 was the 10-17 17:33 deploy (SDK 1.30.0 — the 1.32.1 bump deployed only at 09:35), so a stale refresh, a big parse, a CPU kill and the dependency bump are all ruled out; /mcp logged nothing. What the code allowed: @hono/mcp's SSE path returns the Response before the tool call runs, so the call ran after the fetch handler returned, kept alive only by the open stream — the one kind of work a Worker may drop, and a dropped call leaves the stream open until the client's timeout, exactly the reading. Fix: routes/mcp.ts answers a POST with one JSON body (enableJsonResponse, spec-allowed, every client accepts both), so the call runs inside the awaited handler; every data tool runs under a 10 s deadline (src/lib/deadline.ts) answering a tool error naming the phase and logging slow_tool_call; the probe tells "body unread (headers arrived)" from no response and bounds its own body read. Version 0.25.2 so /v1/health names the build. Cause not proven; the next hang is readable on both sides.
